title: Phenols & ethers
examples: What makes phenol more acidic than benzene?
Can you explain the reaction mechanism for the nitration of phenol?
How does the structure of the ether group affect reactivity?

explain.say: Today we are looking at phenols and ethers in organic chemistry.
First we will discuss the acidity of phenol compared to phenol derivatives.
Phenols are acidic because the resulting phenoxide ion is stabilized by resonance.
Next we look at the electrophilic substitution reactions on the phenol ring.
The ether group is generally electron donating, activating the ring towards substitution.
In reality, when you react phenol with bromine water, you get a white precipitate.

faq.q: Why is phenol more acidic than simple alcohols?
faq.a: Phenol is more acidic because the phenoxide ion formed can be stabilized by resonance within the benzene ring structure. This resonance stabilization is not possible when forming an alkoxide ion from an alcohol.
asks: Compare the acidity of phenol and ethanol.

faq.q: How does the ether group affect the reactivity of the phenol ring?
faq.a: The ether group is an electron-donating group, which increases the electron density of the benzene ring. This makes the ring more reactive towards electrophilic substitution reactions. It directs incoming groups to the ortho and para positions.
asks: Does the ether group activate the ring?
What is the effect of an ether on electrophilic substitution?

faq.q: What type of reaction occurs when phenol reacts with bromine water?
faq.a: The reaction is an electrophilic substitution, specifically a halogenation. Phenol reacts readily with bromine water to form a white precipitate, indicating the substitution of hydrogen atoms by bromine atoms at the ortho and para positions.
asks: What color is the precipitate with bromine?
Does phenol react with bromine water?

faq.q: Is the acidity of phenol dependent on substituents?
faq.a: Yes, substituents can affect acidity. Electron-withdrawing groups increase acidity, while electron-donating groups decrease it, by altering the stability of the phenoxide anion.
asks: How do substituents change phenol acidity?
What affects the pKa of phenol?

faq.q: Can the ether group be cleaved under mild conditions?
faq.a: Ethers are generally stable, but they can be cleaved by strong acids with heating, or by specific reagents like boron tribromide. This process breaks the C-O bond.
asks: How do you break an ether bond?

facts: Phenol is significantly more acidic than benzene.
The acidity of phenol is due to resonance stabilization of the phenoxide ion.
Electrophilic substitution on phenol is highly favored.
The ether group is an activating, ortho-para directing group.

quiz.say: Which species is most stable: the phenoxide ion or the alkoxide ion?
quiz.why: The negative charge on the phenoxide ion can be delocalized into the benzene ring through resonance, which greatly stabilizes the ion.

wrong.0: The negative charge on an alkoxide ion is localized only on the oxygen atom, offering less stability.
wrong.1: Benzene is neutral and does not carry the negative charge that needs stabilizing.
wrong.2: The neutral phenol molecule is less stable than its conjugate base, the phenoxide ion.

quiz.say: When phenol reacts with bromine water, what color change is observed?
quiz.why: The reaction substitutes the hydrogen atoms at the ortho and para positions with bromine atoms, forming a visible white precipitate.

wrong.1: Brown color is often associated with excess bromine, but the reaction itself yields a solid.
wrong.2: Phenol is highly reactive and undergoes a noticeable reaction with bromine water.
wrong.3: Yellow solutions might indicate other impurities, but the characteristic product is white.

quiz.say: If an ether group is attached to phenol, how does this affect acidity compared to phenol?
quiz.why: The ether oxygen donates electron density, which destabilizes the resulting phenoxide ion, making the acid weaker.

wrong.0: Electron-donating groups always increase acidity, which is incorrect for resonance effects.
wrong.1: The oxygen atom in the ether group has lone pairs that participate in resonance, causing a measurable effect.
wrong.2: The effect is on acidity, not just on general reactivity.
